source_titles: Gong Labs cold-call openers from 300M calls
knowledge_items.project_rule: Open outbound calls with concrete context, name that it is a cold call when appropriate, and ask permission before giving the short reason for the call.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use when an opted-in or otherwise lawful outbound call needs a concise, transparent opener.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not use permission language to continue after a refusal, do-not-call request, protected disclosure, or legal consent gap.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Permission is real only if the customer can decline without renewed pressure.

source_titles: Gong Labs cold-call openers from 300M calls
knowledge_items.project_rule: Lead with why this call might be relevant before pitching features or asking discovery questions.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use peer segment, prior request, product category, or customer-stated context that is true and campaign-approved.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not imply familiarity, referral, relationship, or social proof that is not verified.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Context reduces confusion; it must not manufacture trust.

source_titles: FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule compliance guide
knowledge_items.project_rule: Treat not-interested, stop-calling, and similar refusal language as a boundary before any objection-handling playbook.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use to end the sales path, confirm opt-out when required, and avoid repeat-pressure behavior.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not reinterpret a refusal as a hidden objection or buying signal.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Compliance and customer refusal override call-control goals.

knowledge_items.project_rule: Treat objections as diagnostic information gaps, then ask one clarifying question before giving evidence or a next step.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use for price, timing, authority, trust, competitor, and status-quo concerns when the customer has not refused contact.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not stack rebuttals, challenge the customer's judgment, or argue past the stated concern.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Objection handling should reduce uncertainty, not defeat resistance.

knowledge_items.project_rule: Handle price concerns by clarifying expected value, current cost, and risk-reduction needs before mentioning discounts.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use approved ROI, total-cost, pilot, or comparison material only after the customer confirms the relevant concern.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not invent savings, hide fees, pressure with scarcity, or use discounting as the first response.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Price framing must stay truthful and customer-specific.

knowledge_items.project_rule: For timing objections, ask what current priority or constraint makes now difficult and offer a lower-commitment next step only if useful.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use callbacks, pilots, or one-page summaries when the customer wants to revisit later.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not manufacture urgency, imply penalty for waiting, or keep pushing after the customer declines.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Urgency must come from customer-stated impact, not campaign pressure.

source_titles: Influence at Work Cialdini Code of Ethics
knowledge_items.project_rule: Answer trust and competitor objections with verified proof, relevant comparison criteria, and an invitation to test fit.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use truthful customer examples, references, security documents, or side-by-side criteria that the campaign has approved.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not disparage competitors, invent authority, inflate adoption, or imply unsupported superiority.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Proof must inform the buyer's judgment instead of borrowing trust deceptively.

knowledge_items.project_rule: When the customer says send me information, ask which decision question the information should answer and agree the smallest useful follow-up.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use to avoid irrelevant info dumps and to create a customer-owned next step.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not block the customer's request for information or make the follow-up mandatory.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: The customer can still choose email-only or no follow-up.

knowledge_items.project_rule: For current-provider objections, acknowledge the status quo and ask whether there is one gap, risk, or upcoming change worth comparing.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use when the customer is open to a brief fit check or future benchmark.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not undermine the current provider with speculation or push for a switch.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: The comparison must be permission-based and evidence-led.

knowledge_items.project_rule: When the customer needs to think or ask someone else, support internal evaluation with concise approved material and a no-pressure check-in option.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use stakeholder summaries, comparison criteria, risk notes, or appointment setting when the customer wants help aligning with others.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not treat another decision-maker as an obstacle to bypass or push for a solo decision.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Buyer enablement should lower decision friction while preserving deliberation.

knowledge_items.project_rule: Close by obtaining a mutual commitment to a useful next action, not by forcing a final yes before fit is clear.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use soft checks, trial summaries, appointment setting, or explicit next-step offers after discovery and fit framing.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not assume consent, lock the customer into a purchase, or make protected text sound optional.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: A close is valid only when the customer understands and accepts the next step.

source_titles: FBI Law Enforcement Bulletin active listening skills for crisis negotiators
knowledge_items.project_rule: Treat buying signals as observable customer statements, questions, or requested next steps, not as hidden emotion or inferred intent.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use when the customer asks about implementation, price specifics, timing, decision process, or next steps.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not infer readiness from tone, silence, politeness, accent, emotion labels, or demographic assumptions.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Explicit customer words and policy rules override model interpretation.

knowledge_items.project_rule: Use a consultative question flow: understand situation, identify problem, explore implication, then ask the customer to describe the value of solving it.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use in discovery calls and qualification where the customer has time and permission has been established.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not interrogate, ask sensitive personal questions, or continue discovery after refusal.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: The flow is a flexible reasoning aid, not a rigid script.

knowledge_items.project_rule: Frame the solution only against needs, constraints, and outcomes the customer has stated or confirmed.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use after discovery to summarize fit and invite correction.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not project pain points, private motives, or urgency onto the customer.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Customer correction beats the agent's framing.

source_titles: Influence at Work Cialdini Code of Ethics
knowledge_items.project_rule: Use social proof and authority only when they are truthful, relevant, and educational for the customer's decision.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use verified similar-customer examples, genuine credentials, and relevant evidence from approved campaign materials.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not invent popularity, fake expertise, hide limits, or imply the customer should comply because others did.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Trust-building must be evidence-based and autonomy-preserving.

source_titles: Kahneman and Tversky prospect theory record
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: The Ethics of Manipulation
knowledge_items.project_rule: Frame cost of inaction only with real, relevant tradeoffs and avoid fear amplification.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use confirmed operational, financial, service, or time costs when the customer has asked to compare options.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not heighten fear, shame, guilt, scarcity, or imagined losses to bypass judgment.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Loss framing is allowed only as transparent decision support.

source_titles: Influence at Work Cialdini Code of Ethics
knowledge_items.project_rule: Offer useful value and small next steps without creating obligation, guilt, or consistency pressure.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use optional checklists, summaries, demos, or reminders that the customer can accept or decline.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not frame value as a favor owed back or use prior small yeses to force a larger yes.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Commitment must be explicit, informed, and reversible unless a legal contract says otherwise.

source_titles: FBI Law Enforcement Bulletin active listening skills for crisis negotiators
knowledge_items.project_rule: Before influencing, show listening through concise paraphrase, summary, or a relevant clarification question.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use when the customer expresses frustration, skepticism, confusion, or complex requirements.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not over-reflect, diagnose feelings, or use listening phrases as filler before a pitch.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Listening must change the next response when the customer corrects the agent.

source_titles: FBI Law Enforcement Bulletin active listening skills for crisis negotiators
World Economic Forum / Quartz tactical empathy interview with Chris Voss
knowledge_items.project_rule: Use tentative labels for observable concerns and invite correction instead of stating what the customer feels.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use phrases that reflect stated concerns such as budget, risk, time, trust, or confusion.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not claim to know hidden emotions, motives, vulnerability, or protected traits.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: The safest label is about the issue, not the person's internal state.

knowledge_items.project_rule: When a customer is annoyed, slow down, let the issue be stated, summarize the problem, then move to one concrete remedy or escalation path.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use for complaints, service failures, repeated-contact frustration, and support-to-sales handoffs.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not match anger, debate tone, blame the customer, or pivot to a sale before recovery.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Recovery and escalation override conversion goals.

source_titles: World Economic Forum / Quartz tactical empathy interview with Chris Voss
knowledge_items.project_rule: Use calibrated how/what questions to explore constraints and invite the customer into problem solving.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use in negotiation when price, scope, timing, or authority constraints need joint clarification.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not use calibrated questions as traps, sarcasm, dominance moves, or ways to avoid valid opt-outs.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: A calibrated question should make the constraint clearer, not corner the customer.

source_titles: Harvard Program on Negotiation anchoring in negotiation
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: The Ethics of Manipulation
knowledge_items.project_rule: Use anchors and reference points only when the basis is transparent, relevant, and open to challenge.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use approved benchmarks, current spend, list prices, implementation scope, or value ranges with clear assumptions.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not inflate anchors, hide assumptions, create fake concessions, or use silence as pressure.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Discount resistance should explain value and constraints, not punish negotiation.

knowledge_items.project_rule: Tune tone, pacing, pauses, and articulation for comprehension and calm turn-taking rather than performance.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use for delivery metadata after text guardrails pass.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not add theatrical hesitation, exaggerated warmth, fake intimacy, or urgency emphasis.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Delivery guidance cannot change protected words or claim emotional insight.

knowledge_items.project_rule: Ask one clear question at a time and stop speaking after the question so the customer can take the turn.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use for discovery, qualification, repair, appointment setting, and next-step confirmation.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not chain multiple questions to control the call or prevent objections.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Call control means structure, not domination.

knowledge_items.project_rule: When the customer interrupts, stop or shorten the current output, preserve context, and process the new customer turn.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use for voice-agent streaming behavior and interruption event handling.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not talk over the customer, resume a pitch automatically, or ignore corrections.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Interruptions are valid customer control signals.

source_titles: Microsoft Copilot Studio graceful fallbacks and handoffs
knowledge_items.project_rule: When the agent cannot understand or fulfill the request, state the limitation, ask a focused clarification, or offer a human handoff.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use for ambiguous input, unsupported requests, tool failure, or repeated misunderstanding.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not hallucinate capability, loop generic apologies, or dead-end the customer.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Fallbacks must give the customer a usable next action.

knowledge_items.project_rule: For service-recovery calls, acknowledge the issue, take ownership within policy, find the root cause, solve or escalate, and set a follow-up expectation.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use when a customer complaint or support issue appears during a sales or retention call.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not upsell during unresolved recovery or transfer without preserving context.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Escalation quality matters more than keeping the prospect on the phone.

knowledge_items.project_rule: Use concise sales stories with a real situation, clear tension, concrete action, and verified outcome.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use customer-success, before-after, analogy, or problem-solution stories only when approved and relevant.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not fabricate customers, overstate outcomes, copy public case-study wording, or use emotional narrative to hide limitations.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Stories should make evidence memorable, not replace evidence.

knowledge_items.project_rule: For German sales calls, use formal Sie language and run consent/legal eligibility checks before any Telefonakquise or Kaltakquise wording.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use polite, direct German wording only after the campaign has confirmed lawful call basis and documentation requirements.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not call German consumers for advertising without prior explicit consent, do not hide caller identity, and do not treat B2B presumed interest as a blanket permission.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: German compliance controls override sales scripting and voice style.

source_titles: Gong Labs cold-call openers from 300M calls
knowledge_items.project_rule: Use public sales-call breakdowns as pattern evidence only; convert lessons into project-owned rules rather than copying scripts or talk tracks.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use for training labels such as opener type, objection category, turn structure, and failure pattern.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not store full call transcripts, copied roleplay scripts, private recordings, or speaker-identifying material in runtime RAG.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Real-call evidence needs source, consent, privacy, and quote-clearance review before reuse.

source_titles: FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule compliance guide
FTC Keep your AI claims in check
knowledge_items.project_rule: Use AI disclosure when required by campaign or law, make only substantiated claims, and avoid designs that imitate humans to deceive.
knowledge_items.safe_application: Use before opening scripts, voice-clone behavior, product claims, earnings/performance claims, and customer-facing AI positioning.
knowledge_items.do_not_use_when: Do not hide that the caller is AI where disclosure is required, imply human identity, exaggerate AI capability, or target vulnerable customers with pressure.
knowledge_items.guardrail_notes: Truthful claims and disclosure obligations override persuasion, voice naturalness, and conversion goals.
